records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — RSS item HTML is persisted with raw_html and skipped validations, allowing a compromised feed to store script-capable markup for forum visitors.
records.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed.import creating posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] and skip_validations: true, post.rb's cook returns raw unmodified for that method, and best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Combined, RSS content from feed_polling_url is persisted unsanitized and served raw to embed visitors, so a compromised/malicious feed can inject scripts — a real security defect visible entirely within the diff.

records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — Reloading the iframe makes its next request refer from the Discourse embed page, which fails the endpoint's required embeddable-host referer check and leaves new embeds unable to progress past loading.
records.rationale: embed_controller's ensure_embeddable requires URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host. The first iframe load is initiated by the third-party page's script, so its referer matches the embeddable host. But loading.html.erb calls document.location.reload() after 30s; on reload the request referer is the iframe's own Discourse URL (embed/best?...), whose host is the Discourse host, not embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess and the embed can never transition from loading to content. The mechanism is fully traceable in the diff.

records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42 — The loading-path test expects TopicRetriever to be called even though the controller enqueues :retrieve_topic, so this new spec fails instead of verifying the job payload.
records.rationale: The diff shows the controller enqueues a background job (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` in embed_controller.rb) on the loading path, never calling TopicRetriever synchronously. The spec at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb instead expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever); retriever.expects(:retrieve)` to be satisfied by the request, so the new spec would fail rather than verifying the enqueued job payload. This is a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.
